0. Introduction — Welcome to Halcyon#

Mutagen is a tabletop roleplaying game about freelancers who rebuild their own bodies to survive a city that is rebuilding itself. There are no races and no classes. The Mutagen pulls you toward one of five Base Forms (Juggernaut, Skitter, Oracle, Alembic or Siren), and you become whatever you graft on along the way: chitin and venom, chrome and wire, or a twitching mix of both. Twice in your career you Evolve, suddenly and violently, into something far bigger. In a fight your body does not always do what you planned; it Surges, offering you a random handful of powers from everything you have ever become.

What You Need#

  • 3–5 players and one Game Master (GM).
  • A d20 per player, plus a few d4, d6, d8, d10, and d12.
  • A character sheet per player (sheets/).
  • Tokens for Juice (coins, beads; 3 per player).

The Setting in One Page#

Thirty years ago the Ostrander Biotech Arcology, a mile-high lab tower in the coastal megacity of Halcyon, cracked open. Millions of litres of Mutagen, a programmable living gel, poured into the water table. We call it the Spill.

Mutagen does one thing: it makes flesh accept change. A dose lets your body grow a new organ, or lets it accept a steel arm without rejection. Untamed, it makes rats fuse into hulks, mould think, and machines grow meat. The national government walled Halcyon off and outsourced the problem.

G.R.A.F.T. (Genetic Response And Field Tactics) is the private contractor that won the cleanup bid. GRAFT does not hire soldiers. It licenses freelancers: people already saturated with Mutagen who can go where clean humans die. You are one of them. GRAFT pays per mission, sells you upgrades at its clinics, and owns everything you bring back.

Factions in a sentence each:

  • GRAFT — your employer. Polite, underfunded, and lying about what's in the samples.
  • Ostrander Remnant — the old company, still alive in the upper arcology, sending sterile "Cleaner" squads to erase evidence.
  • The Children of the Bloom — a faith that believes the Spill is the next step of evolution, and that you are halfway there.
  • The Scrapjacks — chrome scavengers who strip the dead (and the living) for parts.
  • The Drowned Wards — ordinary people living in the flooded lower city, trying not to become anything.

Tone#

Gritty, weird, and a little funny. Bodies are strange and that is not tragic by default; it can be glorious, gross, or both. Missions are short and dangerous. The city is enormous and mostly unexplored.

The Big Ideas#

  1. One roll for everything: d20 + Stat (+ Rank) against a number. (Chapter 1)
  2. Emotive stats: Grit, Moxie, Nerve, Gumption, Chutzpah. They describe how you do things, not what you are. (Chapter 2)
  3. You are your Form and your Augments: five Base Forms, each growing along three of six 10-node skill trees (Hide, Limbs, Senses, Glands, Wiring, Mind), each tree grown as Bio or installed as Chrome. Evolutions at levels 4 and 7 transform your body and your numbers. (Chapter 2A, Chapter 3)
  4. Surges: you build a personal list of combat powers from mix-and-match parts. Each fight, dice decide which few are ready. Using them is optional; your weapons and Augments always work. (Chapter 4)
  5. Flux: every Surge pushes your body closer to Overload, where the Mutagen takes the wheel. (Chapter 5)
  6. Player-facing dice: the GM rarely rolls. Players roll to hit, and players roll to dodge. (Chapter 6)
  7. One mission, one level: a campaign runs 10 missions, levels 1 to 10. (Chapter 7)

Prefer one book? The Mutagen Rulebook compiles all of these chapters into a single numbered document with a full table of contents and a glossary (also as a print-ready PDF).

1. Core Rules#

Mutagen uses one roll for everything.

The Roll#

Roll d20 + Stat (+ Rank, if it applies). Meet or beat the target number to succeed.

  • Stat is one of your five stats: −1 to +3 at level 1, rising to as high as +8 as your Base Form Evolves (Chapter 2A), +10 in Final Form.
  • Rank is your level-based bonus: Rank = half your level, rounded up (1 at level 1–2, up to 5 at level 9–10).
  • You always add Rank to attack rolls and defense rolls.
  • You add Rank to a check only if one of your Knacks applies.
  • Ties go to the player.

There are three kinds of roll:

RollWhenTarget
CheckYou try something risky outside of attacking or defendingA DC set by the GM
AttackYou try to hurt somethingThe target's Guard
DefenseSomething tries to hurt youThe attacker's Threat Number (TN)

The GM almost never rolls. Enemies don't roll to hit you; you roll to avoid them (see Combat).

Difficulty (DC)#

DCDifficultyExample
—TrivialNo roll. Just do it.
10EasyClimb a chain-link fence in the rain
13StandardTalk a Ward guard into letting you pass
16HardHotwire an Ostrander security door
19ExtremeLeap between two moving maglev cars
22MutantHold a collapsing ceiling up with your bare (augmented) back
25MonstrousOutrun a maglev; shout down a riot; read a stranger's mind from across a plaza
28MythicOnly an Evolved freelancer's primary stat even has a chance

Only roll when failure is interesting. On a failure, the GM picks a consequence: you fail, you succeed at a cost, or the situation gets worse.

DCs don't scale with level. A locked door is DC 16 whether you're level 1 or 9. Evolved freelancers simply are better at things their Form is good at: by level 7, a primary stat of +8 passes a Hard check on an 8+. Raise the stakes instead of the DC: higher-level missions put Extreme and Mutant obstacles in your path, and ask for checks with your weak stats. See Running the Game.

Knacks#

A Knack is a short, specific phrase describing something you're trained in: Street Medicine, Lying to Cops, Old Ostrander Tech, Parkour, Sewer Navigation. When a Knack fits a check, add your Rank. If it's arguable, the GM decides; lean toward yes for narrow Knacks. You start with 3 Knacks and gain more as you level.

Advantage and Disadvantage#

Advantage: roll 2d20, keep the higher. Disadvantage: roll 2d20, keep the lower. They don't stack; if you have both, roll normally.

Player-facing rule: if an enemy would have advantage on an attack, the defending player rolls their defense with disadvantage, and vice versa.

Natural 20s and 1s#

  • Natural 20 on an attack: a Crit. Roll the damage dice twice.
  • Natural 20 on a defense: you avoid it entirely, and the attacker is Exposed (see Conditions).
  • Natural 20 on a check: success, plus a bonus the GM describes.
  • Natural 1 on anything: automatic failure.

Group Checks#

When the whole party attempts something together (sneaking past, hauling a door), everyone rolls. If at least half succeed, the group succeeds.

Helping#

To help someone, describe how and use your Action (in combat) or just do it (outside combat). They roll with advantage.

Juice#

Juice is a reward token for great play: clever plans, bold roleplay, making the table laugh, or suffering for the story. The GM hands it out.

  • You start each session with 1 Juice and can hold 3.
  • Spend 1 Juice to do one of:
    • Reroll any d20 you just rolled (use the new result).
    • Choose a Prime: set one of your Sequence dice to any result you want (see Surges).
    • Shrug: end one condition on yourself.

Stats at a Glance#

StatIt's aboutRolls it covers
GritToughness, force, refusal to fall overPower melee, lifting, breaking, Endure defense, Max HP
MoxieDaring, speed, flair under pressureFinesse melee, sprinting, sneaking, climbing, Dodge defense, initiative
NerveCool head, steady hands, willpowerRanged attacks, noticing things, Resist defense, Flux Limit
GumptionResourcefulness, know-how, figuring it outTech, medicine, science, hacking, Analyze, Patch
ChutzpahAudacity, charm, nerve-in-your-facePersuade, lie, intimidate, perform, Taunt, Rally, psionic Surges

Rest#

  • Breather (about an hour, somewhere quiet): regain half your Max HP, Flux drops to 0. You can take two Breathers between Lockdowns.
  • Lockdown (8 hours in a safe place): regain all HP, Flux to 0, end temporary Overload effects, reset Breathers and "once per Lockdown" abilities.

Time and Distance#

Combat runs in rounds (about 6 seconds). Distances are in feet. Play them either way (Positioning): in theatre of the mind use Close (5 ft, touching), Near (up to 30 ft, one move), Far (up to 120 ft) and Distant (beyond); on a grid, 1 square = 5 ft and diagonals count as one square.

Golden Rules#

  1. Specific beats general. An Augment or Surge that says otherwise wins.
  2. Round down unless told otherwise (minimum 1 for damage).
  3. The GM decides when the rules are unclear, then writes it down and moves on.

2. Character Creation#

You don't pick a race or a class. You pick what the Mutagen is turning you into (your Base Form), where you came from (Origin), and what you've done to your body (Augments). It takes about 30 minutes; the web builder does the maths for you.

Step by Step#

  1. Concept. One sentence. "Ex-cop with a shotgun arm who can't stop apologising."
  2. Base Form. Pick one of the five Base Forms: Juggernaut, Skitter, Oracle, Alembic or Siren. It sets your best stats, your three trees and how you'll Evolve.
  3. Stats. Your Form gives +3 (primary), +2 (secondary) and +1 (tertiary). Put +0 and −1 in the other two stats, in either order.
  4. Origin. Pick or roll one (below). Write down its Knack and Perk.
  5. Knacks. Write two more Knacks (3 total). Keep them narrow.
  6. Augments. Take 6 nodes from your Form's trees (chapter 3): the Root + 2 Tier I nodes of your primary tree, the Root + 1 Tier I node of your secondary tree, and the Root of your tertiary tree. For each tree, choose its Material: Bio or Chrome.
  7. Surges. Build 3 Surges (Chapter 4) and number them 1–3 on your Sequence. Slot 4 is Wild (Lab Escapees build a 4th instead).
  8. Gear. Take one Kit from Gear and 50 Scrip.
  9. Fill in the numbers (below).
  10. Drive. Answer three questions: Why did you take the Mutagen? What do you want before the campaign ends? Who in Halcyon do you owe, or hate?

Derived Numbers (Level 1)#

NumberValue
Rank1 (half your level, rounded up)
Max HP12 + (2 × Grit) + 5 per level after 1st. Recalculate when Grit changes (it does at each Evolution).
ArmorFrom gear and the Hide tree (max 4, unless a node says otherwise)
Speed30 ft
Flux Limit4 + Rank + Nerve (minimum 4; Splice −1)
Sequence died4
Prime2
Signature SurgesNone yet (the first comes at Evolution I, level 4)
Juice1 (max 3)
DefensesDodge = Moxie + Rank, Endure = Grit + Rank, Resist = Nerve + Rank

The Five Stats#

Stats are attitudes, not body parts. A gangly kid can have huge Grit; it means they won't stay down. Your Base Form decides which attitudes the Mutagen feeds, and every Evolution feeds them more (up to +8).

  • Grit — "I'm still standing." Raw force and stubborn endurance. Use it to smash, lift, grapple, hit hard in melee, and Endure poison, blasts, and crushing blows. It raises your HP.
  • Moxie — "Watch this." Nimble daring. Use it to sprint, climb, sneak, tumble, fight with finesse weapons, and Dodge attacks you can see coming. It sets initiative.
  • Nerve — "Breathe. Aim." Composure and willpower. Use it to shoot, notice, track, keep calm, and Resist fear, mind control, and psychic attack. It holds your Mutagen together (your Flux Limit).
  • Gumption — "Hand me that wrench." Resourceful know-how. Use it to fix, hack, patch wounds, recall lore, read a situation, and Analyze enemies.
  • Chutzpah — "You and what army?" Shameless audacity. Use it to persuade, lie, threaten, perform, lead, Taunt enemies, Rally allies, and power psionic Dread Surges.

Which defense? Attacks you can sidestep (claws, bullets, spit) are Dodge. Things you must take on the chin (gas, explosions you can't escape, disease, grabs) are Endure. Things that attack your mind (fear, hacking your wetware, psychic screams) are Resist. Every threat's stat block names the defense.

Origins (roll d6 or choose)#

d6OriginKnackPerk
1Spill-Born — raised in the flooded Wards.ScavengingAdvantage on Endure against poison, disease, and anything that adds Flux to you.
2Corporate Washout — ex-Ostrander staff, fired or fled.Corporate ProtocolStart with +100 Scrip. Once per mission, name an old contact who can open one door.
3Lab Escapee — you were the experiment.Lab ScienceYou know one extra Surge at every level (it fills a Wild slot; no effect once your Sequence has no Wild slots). It never adds a Signature Surge.
4Clinic Rat — a street surgeon raised you, or still owns you.Street MedicineYour Patch action heals +Rank extra HP, and removing Scars or Faults costs you half (the doc wants favours instead).
5Ward Militia — you held the barricades.Squad Tactics+2 to your roll in group initiative checks. Once per combat, take Brace as a Quick action.
6Bloom Convert — the Children took you in.Bloom LoreOnce per Lockdown, reroll an Overload result and choose either result.

Knack Examples#

Parkour, Knife Fighting, Ostrander Security, Drone Piloting, Sewer Routes, Fast Talk, Interrogation, Chemistry, Mutant Biology, Salvage Appraisal, Street Medicine, Black-Market Contacts, Crowd Work, Lockpicking, Swimming, Gambling, Old Halcyon History, Cooking Anything, Bloom Scripture, Explosives.

A Knack should be something you could teach in a weekend course or learn on the street in a year. "Everything Physical" is not a Knack.

Example: Vex (Level 1)#

  • Concept: Wiry Spill-Born courier with mantis claws who runs messages through gang turf.
  • Form: Skitter. Moxie +3, Gumption +2, Grit +1; she puts Nerve +0 and Chutzpah −1.
  • Origin: Spill-Born (Scavenging). Knacks: Parkour, Gang Turf.
  • Augments (6): Wiring (Bio): Quickened (Root), Capacitor, Slipstream. Limbs (Bio): Natural Weapons (Root), Spring Legs. Senses (Bio): Keen (Root). She is all Bio, so Knit heals her 1 × 3 = 3 HP after each fight.
  • Surge parts: base (Strike, Bolt, Infuse, Kinetic) + Wiring (Shock, Blaze, Haste) + Limbs (Wave, Snare) + Senses (Glare, Veil).
  • Surges: 1 Mantis Lunge (Strike + Kinetic, Moxie), 2 Live Wire (Bolt + Shock, Moxie via Wiring), 3 Slip Veil (Infuse + Veil). 4 = Wild.
  • Gear: Sneak kit (two knives, suppressed pistol, Breach kit), Light armor.
  • Numbers: HP 14, Armor 1, Speed 50 ft (Quickened + Spring Legs), Limit 5 (4 + 1 + 0), Dodge +4, Endure +2, Resist +1. Claws: +4 to hit, 1d8+3, +1d8 Shock once per turn (Capacitor).
  • Her Evolution I (level 4, Mantis): Moxie +5, Gumption +3, Grit +2, Nerve +1, Chutzpah +0; Prime 3, d8 Sequence, Mantis Reflex, and a Signature Surge (she'll pick Live Wire).

2A. Base Forms & Evolution#

The Mutagen doesn't make you anything. It makes you into something: one of five shapes the city's freelancers keep turning into. That shape is your Base Form. It sets your best stats and the three Augment trees you grow along. Twice in your career it Evolves, suddenly and violently, into something bigger.

Choosing a Form#

FormPrimary +3Secondary +2Tertiary +1You place +0 and −1 inPrimary treeSecondaryTertiaryIn one line
JuggernautGritNerveChutzpahMoxie, GumptionHideLimbsGlands"I don't move. You do."
SkitterMoxieGumptionGritNerve, ChutzpahWiringLimbsSenses"You blinked. I was already there."
OracleNerveChutzpahMoxieGrit, GumptionSensesMindWiring"I saw you coming. Three days ago."
AlembicGumptionGritNerveMoxie, ChutzpahGlandsHideMind"Hold still. This will either cure you or kill it."
SirenChutzpahMoxieGumptionGrit, NerveMindWiringLimbs"Everybody look at me."
  • Stats: your Form fixes your +3, +2 and +1. You put +0 in one of the other two stats and −1 in the last.
  • Trees: you take nodes only from your Form's three trees (chapter 3): 3 in the primary, 2 in the secondary and 1 in the tertiary at level 1.
  • Material: for each tree, choose Bio or Chrome, as before. A Chrome Oracle and a Bio Oracle both see everything, but one does it with lenses and the other with eyes.
  • Every stat is primary for one Form, secondary for one and tertiary for one.

Stages#

StageLevelsPrimarySecondaryTertiaryDump (+0)Dump (−1)
Base1–3+3+2+1+0−1
Evolution I4–6+5+3+2+1+0
Evolution II7–10+8+4+3+2+1
Final Form (active)10+10+4+3+2+1

There are no other stat increases. Your stats only change when your body does.

What an Evolution Gives#

Evolution I happens at level 4 and Evolution II at level 7. Each one gives you all of the following:

Evolution I (level 4)Evolution II (level 7)
Stats+2 primary, +1 every other stat+3 primary, +1 every other stat
Prime2 → 33 → 4
Sequence died6 → d8d8 → d12 (skips d10)
Signature SurgeYour first Signature SurgeYour second Signature Surge
Evolution nodeYour Form's level 4 nodeYour Form's level 7 node
LookYour Form's Evolution I lookYour Form's Evolution II look

Your Max HP, defenses, Flux Limit and attacks all rise with the new stats. Right after an Evolution, fights get noticeably easier. The threats of the next few missions catch up with you (see Threats).

Signature Surges#

A Signature Surge is the power your new body was built around. It's always there.

  • Build it from your Surge parts like any Surge (chapter 4), with Twists as your Rank allows. Name it after what your body does now.
  • Write it in a Signature box, not on your Sequence. It doesn't count toward your Surges known, your Prime, or your Primed maximum.
  • It is always ready. It's Primed at the start of every combat. After you Unleash it, it's Primed again at the start of your next turn, so you can use each Signature once per round.
  • It costs its normal Flux (1 + 1 per Twist). It can't be Amped by doubles; only Emergence and Final Form Amp it.
  • Missed? A missed Strike or Bolt Signature is still ready next turn, like any Signature.
  • Changing it: when you level up (from level 5), you may rebuild one Signature Surge.
  • Flux is the limit. You can now Surge every turn, but every Surge pushes you toward Overload. Pace yourself, or plan your Overloads.

Emergence: the moment it happens#

You gain the level, and its numbers, at the debrief like any other level. The metamorphosis plays out on screen. At the start of your first turn in the first combat of your next mission, you Emerge. If you and the GM agree on an earlier moment of terror (a fall, a fire, a friend going Down), it happens then instead.

  1. Describe it. Use your Form's look below: what splits, what grows, what you hear.
  2. Gain temporary HP equal to 2 × your level.
  3. Every enemy within 30 ft that can see you is Shaken (Bosses ignore this).
  4. The first time you Unleash your new Signature Surge this combat, it's Amped (0 Flux).

Emerging takes no action. It happens once per Evolution.

GM tip. Before the mission, ask the player: "What's the first sign it's happening?" Plant it in the Approach scene: an itch under the plating, a second heartbeat, a voice in the wiring. Optional downtime Chrysalis scene: see Running the Game.

Final Form (level 10)#

Your third and last stage. At level 10 you take your Form's Final look for good. Once per Lockdown, at the start of a combat (after Priming), you may enter Final Form until the combat ends:

  • +2 to your primary stat (to +10).
  • Prime two extra Surges right away (your Primed maximum rises to match).
  • Every Surge you Unleash is Amped (0 Flux), Signature Surges included.

The Five Forms#

Juggernaut#

Primary Grit · Secondary Nerve · Tertiary Chutzpah · Dump Moxie and Gumption · Trees: Hide (primary), Limbs (secondary), Glands (tertiary)

"I don't move. You do." The Mutagen decided you should be unkillable and started stacking. Juggernauts hold doorways, carry the wounded, and end arguments by standing in them. Grit and Nerve make them hard to hurt and harder to scare, and a little Chutzpah helps them loom. They're slow off the mark and not much for book-learning.

  • Play it if you want to be the wall: Taunt, intercept, and take the hit meant for your friend.
  • Evolution nodes: Siege Hide (level 4): +1 Armor, Armor max 6, reach 10 ft, counts as Huge. Fortress (level 7): allies near you take half Area damage, and once per round you take an ally's lethal hit.
StageNameBioChrome
BaseJuggernautThick neck, heavy brow, knuckles armoured with horn. Your skin has the give of a car tyre.Subdermal plates you can feel through your shirt; a spine brace that whines when you stand.
Evolution IRampartYou grow a foot in a night. Your back splits into overlapping bone slabs; your forearms swell into shields.Bulkhead plates bolt over shoulders and chest; your joints are hydraulic now, and they hiss.
Evolution IIColossusNine feet of keratin and scar tissue. Horns, a domed skull, a heartbeat people feel through the floor.A walking bunker: riveted armour, a face behind a visor slit, treads of steel on your soles.
FinalCitadelStone-hard ridges, moss in the cracks, small things nesting in you. You are a place.Siren lights, warning stencils, a hatch in your chest. Ostrander would classify you as infrastructure.

Skitter#

Primary Moxie · Secondary Gumption · Tertiary Grit · Dump Nerve and Chutzpah · Trees: Wiring (primary), Limbs (secondary), Senses (tertiary)

"You blinked. I was already there." The Mutagen took your nerves and set them on fire. Skitters are the fastest thing in any room: clever with their hands, wiry, and impossible to pin down. They're also jumpy, tactless and short on Flux; their Nerve is the first thing to go.

  • Play it if you want to dart in, Daze, dart out, and act more often than anyone else.
  • Evolution nodes: Mantis Reflex (level 4): two Reactions per round, and full-damage Reflex Spikes. Lightning Step (level 7): a half-dice weapon attack as a Quick action after you Unleash.
StageNameBioChrome
BaseSkitterLong limbs, twitchy hands, pupils that never settle; you're warm to the touch.Reflex jacks at the base of the skull; fingertips with steel contacts that spark when you're nervous.
Evolution IMantisYour forearms fold into barbed hooks; your knees bend backwards; you smell like ozone.Synthetic muscle cables under translucent skin, and a capacitor hump between your shoulders.
Evolution IIWraithGlassy wing-cases that hum, faceted eyes, lightning crawling along your veins.You blur when you move; a plasma coil glows through your ribs; you leave scorch-prints.
FinalLivewireBarely solid: a figure of arcs and chitin that's always slightly somewhere else.A human-shaped storm in a chrome cage, held together by a magnetic field.

Oracle#

Primary Nerve · Secondary Chutzpah · Tertiary Moxie · Dump Grit and Gumption · Trees: Senses (primary), Mind (secondary), Wiring (tertiary)

"I saw you coming. Three days ago." The Mutagen gave you too much input, and you learned to stay calm inside it. Oracles see everything, steady everyone and hold the most Flux of any Form (their high Nerve raises their Flux Limit). They're light on their feet but physically fragile and impractical; their aim isn't.

  • Play it if you want to shoot from a rooftop, spot every weakness, and decide which way the dice fall.
  • Evolution nodes: Foresight (level 4): each round, an Omen d20 that can replace any nearby d20. Thousand Eyes (level 7): Target Lock on three creatures, no surprise or Blindness nearby, wider Crits.
StageNameBioChrome

Alembic#

Primary Gumption · Secondary Grit · Tertiary Nerve · Dump Moxie and Chutzpah · Trees: Glands (primary), Hide (secondary), Mind (tertiary)

"Hold still. This will either cure you or kill it." The Mutagen made you a laboratory. Alembics brew medicine and poison in their own bodies, stay standing in toxic air, and keep the whole crew alive. They're slow, tough and steady-handed, with a bedside manner best described as blunt.

  • Play it if you want to heal, poison, and out-think the problem.
  • Evolution nodes: Transmute (level 4): your Toxin and Corrode riders apply both Poisoned and Exposed, and your healing restores more. Panacea (level 7): once per combat, heal everyone nearby and end their conditions.

BaseAlembicGlands swelling at the throat and wrists; you sweat something sweet-smelling and faintly green.Injector ports along your forearms, and a hip-mounted reservoir with a gauge.

Siren#

Primary Chutzpah · Secondary Moxie · Tertiary Gumption · Dump Grit and Nerve · Trees: Mind (primary), Wiring (secondary), Limbs (tertiary)

"Everybody look at me." The Mutagen made you impossible to ignore. Sirens command attention: they talk past guards, Taunt whole rooms, and bend minds. They're quick enough to dodge the attention they draw and sharp enough to improvise, but fragile, reckless, and the first to Overload (their low Nerve means a low Flux Limit).

  • Play it if you want to lead, talk, Taunt and control the battlefield.
  • Evolution nodes: Siren Song (level 4): a Quick mass Taunt that sends every Taunted enemy at you or an ally you name (usually your Juggernaut), at −2 TN. Crown of Will (level 7): once per combat, a non-Boss fights for you.

FinalCrownedToo beautiful to look at directly; people weep, kneel or flee.A living billboard and a broadcast tower; your face is on every screen, saying your name.

3. Augment Trees#

Your Augments are what you've done to your body. Your Base Form (chapter 2A) decides which three trees you grow along: a primary tree you master, a secondary you lean on, and a tertiary you dabble in. There are six trees, and each one is a body system you've rebuilt. Each can be grown (Bio) or installed (Chrome).

TreeStatRoleUnlocksPrimary ofSecondary ofTertiary of
HideGritTank, protectorPulse (Shape), Quake, ShellJuggernautAlembic—
LimbsGrit / MoxieMelee, grappler, moverWave (Shape), Snare—Juggernaut, SkitterSiren
SensesNerveSniper, scout, spotterGlare, VeilOracle—Skitter
GlandsGumptionChemist, healer, attritionBurst (Shape), Toxin, Corrode, MendAlembic—Juggernaut
WiringMoxieSpeed, reflexes, shockShock, Blaze, HasteSkitterSirenOracle
MindChutzpahPsionics, hacking, controlDread, LinkSirenOracleAlembic

How Trees Work#

  • Ten nodes per tree: a Root, four Tier I nodes, four Tier II nodes, and an Apex. A Form's primary tree also holds that Form's two Evolution nodes.
  • You only take nodes from your Form's three trees.
  • Gates:
NodeNeeds
RootNothing. You take all three Roots at level 1.
Tier IThe tree's Root
Tier IILevel 4+ and 3 nodes already in that tree
ApexLevel 7+, 6 other nodes in that tree, and it must be your primary or secondary tree
Evolution nodeYour Form, at level 4 (Evolution I) or level 7 (Evolution II). Granted automatically.

"Nodes in that tree" counts your standard nodes (Root, Tier I, Tier II); Evolution nodes don't count toward a gate.

  • Scaling. Nodes scale with your Rank; you never need a "greater" version. A node is taken once.
  • Push. Some nodes say Push: you may gain 1 Flux to get the extra effect (Chapter 5).
  • Unlocks. Each tree unlocks Surge parts (Chapter 4) the moment you take its Root. Since you take all three Roots at level 1, your Form fixes your Surge parts.

Gaining Nodes#

WhenPrimary treeSecondary or tertiary tree
Level 13 nodes (Root + 2)2 nodes in the secondary (Root + 1) and 1 node in the tertiary (its Root)
Each level after+1 node, automatically. You always get it, and you choose which.+1 node in your secondary or tertiary tree (your choice)
Level 4 and 7+ your Form's Evolution node (on top of the pick)—
  • Primary tree full? Its 10 standard nodes fill up at level 8. From level 9, the automatic primary pick overflows into your secondary or tertiary tree.
  • Totals: 2 × level + 4 nodes, plus Evolution nodes: 6 at level 1, 13 at level 4, 20 at level 7, 26 at level 10.
  • Respec. When you level up, you may swap one node for another of the same pick type that you qualify for. The clinic rips it out.

Material: Bio or Chrome#

When you take a tree's Root, choose its Material: grown or installed. Every node in that tree shares it. Material changes how the tree looks and adds the rules below. (v0.1 called this "Form"; that word now means your Base Form.)

MaterialLooks likePerkCost
Bio (grown)Chitin, scales, extra eyes, glands, tentacles, glowing veinsKnit: at the end of each combat, and when you take a Breather, regain HP equal to Rank × your number of Bio trees.Your Overloads roll on the Bloom table.
Chrome (installed)Plates, pistons, optics, ports, wiring, servo-armsFirmware: once per combat, right after you Prime, you may swap one Primed Surge for any Surge you know that uses a part unlocked by one of your Chrome trees (base parts alone don't count).Your Overloads roll on the Glitch table. You roll defense with disadvantage against Shock attacks. Upkeep: 25 Scrip per Chrome tree each mission (GRAFT prepays your first), or start the mission with +1 Flux per unpaid tree.
Splice (you have both)Meat and metal fighting for the same bodyOverload: roll on both tables, then choose one result. Each tree keeps its own Material rules.Your Flux Limit is −1 (after the minimum of 4).

Your Evolutions follow your Materials: a Bio Juggernaut's Rampart stage grows bone slabs, a Chrome one bolts on bulkheads.

Your Form decides your trees, but which nodes you take decides your role.

Hide — the body as a fortress#

Bio: chitin plates, scales, rubbery blubber, bark-skin. Chrome: dermal plating, kinetic mesh, ablative shell.

Stat: Grit · Role: tank, protector · Unlocks: Pulse (Shape), Quake, Shell · Primary tree of: Juggernaut · Secondary of: Alembic

← Augment Trees

Root#

  • Plating. +1 Armor (+2 from Rank 3). Armor from all sources maxes at 4, unless a node says otherwise.

Tier I (needs the Root)#

  • Thick. +2 Max HP per level (count past levels too).
  • Barbs. When an enemy's melee attack damages you, it takes 2 × Rank damage.
  • Anchor. You can't be knocked Prone, pushed or pulled against your will. You roll defense with advantage against attacks whose rider is Held.
  • Shoulder Check. Once per turn, you can Grapple or Shove as a Quick action.

Tier II (needs level 4+ and 3 nodes in this tree)#

  • Adaptive. When you take Blaze, Shock, Toxin, Corrode or Psychic damage, you resist that type (half damage) until combat ends. One type at a time; a new type replaces the old.
  • Bulwark. Reaction: when an ally within 10 ft is targeted by a Single attack, you become the target instead and roll your own defense. Push: roll it with advantage.
  • Living Wall. Allies adjacent to you get +1 to defense rolls (+2 from Rank 4). It doesn't stack with another Living Wall.
  • Menace. You can Taunt as a Quick action, using Grit in place of Chutzpah. You get +2 to defense rolls against creatures you have Taunted.

Apex (needs level 7+, 6 other nodes in this tree, and this must be your primary or secondary tree)#

  • Unbreakable. Once per round, when you fail a defense roll, Push to take half damage and ignore its rider. Your Armor maximum is 5.

Evolution nodes (Juggernaut only; granted automatically)#

  • Siege Hide (level 4, Evolution I). Your hide thickens into overlapping slabs. +1 Armor, and your Armor maximum is 6. Your melee reach is 10 ft, and you count as Huge (non-Huge creatures can't knock you Prone or push you).
  • Fortress (level 7, Evolution II). You are terrain now. Allies within 10 ft of you take half damage from Area attacks (after their own defense roll). Reaction: once per round, when an ally within 30 ft would drop to 0 HP, you take that damage instead (your Armor applies).

Limbs — claws, legs, and too many arms#

Bio: claws, mantis blades, tentacles, extra arms, digitigrade legs. Chrome: piston arms, mono-blades, grapple lines, servo-arms, hydraulic legs.

Stat: Grit or Moxie · Role: melee, grappler, mover · Unlocks: Wave (Shape), Snare · Secondary tree of: Juggernaut, Skitter · Tertiary of: Siren

Limbs is the shared body tree. It is never a Form's primary tree, so it has no Evolution nodes. Its Apex is open to the Juggernaut and the Skitter, who have it as their secondary tree.

← Augment Trees

Root#

  • Natural Weapons. Claws, blades or pistons: a melee weapon (d8, Grit or Moxie) that can't be disarmed and doesn't need a free hand.

Tier I (needs the Root)#

  • Extra Arm. A third limb. Hold one more item, and draw, stow or interact without using your Quick action. Once per turn, when you hit with a melee attack, deal +1 damage die (one more of that attack's dice). Push: also knock the target Prone (not Huge).
  • Grapnel. Your melee reach is 10 ft. As your Move, you can pull yourself up to 30 ft to any surface you can see, or yank an unheld object to your hand.
  • Spring Legs. +10 ft speed. Jump 20 ft long or 10 ft high as part of your move, climb at full speed, and take half falling damage.
  • Lash Tail. You can make an Opportunity Strike when an enemy enters your melee reach, as well as when it leaves. A hit from an Opportunity Strike knocks a non-Huge target Prone.

Tier II (needs level 4+ and 3 nodes in this tree)#

  • Crusher Grip. Once per turn when you hit with a natural weapon, the target is Held. Huge creatures and Bosses require a Push.
  • Rend. Your natural weapons' die becomes d10 (d12 from Rank 4).
  • Pounce. Once per turn, if you move at least 15 ft toward a creature and then hit it with a melee attack, it's knocked Prone (not Huge), and you can Grapple it as a Quick action.
  • Many Hands. Help is a Quick action for you. You can hold a second creature Held while you already hold one.

Apex (needs level 7+, 6 other nodes in this tree, and this must be your primary or secondary tree)#

  • Flurry. When you take the Attack action with natural weapons, make a second attack with half the damage dice (round up).

Senses — eyes everywhere#

Bio: compound eyes, pit organs, bat ears, whiskers, a third eye. Chrome: optic suites, targeting HUD, radar, audio filters.

Stat: Nerve · Role: sniper, scout, spotter · Unlocks: Glare, Veil · Primary tree of: Oracle · Tertiary of: Skitter

← Augment Trees

Root#

  • Keen. See in darkness out to 60 ft. Advantage on checks to notice hidden things. Bright light can't Blind you.

Tier I (needs the Root)#

  • Target Lock. Quick: mark a creature you can see. Once per turn, your attack against it deals +1 damage die (one more of that attack's dice). The mark lasts until combat ends or you mark another.
  • Threat Sense. You and your group can't be surprised. Reaction: when an ally within 30 ft makes a defense roll, add your Nerve to it (declare before rolling).
  • Analyzer. You can Analyze as a Quick action once per turn.
  • Echolocation. You sense creatures within 30 ft without sight. You can't be Blinded against anything within that range, and hidden or invisible creatures there are revealed to you.

Tier II (needs level 4+ and 3 nodes in this tree)#

  • Long Sight. Double the range of your ranged attacks and ranged Surges. Ignore partial cover. Read lips at 300 ft.
  • Weak Spot. When you Analyze a creature, its Armor and Resistances don't apply to anyone's damage until the end of its next turn.
  • Spotter. Quick, once per round: an ally within 60 ft who can hear you gets advantage on its next attack against a creature you can see.
  • Hair Trigger. When a combat starts, after Priming and before anyone else acts, you may make one ranged weapon attack.

Apex (needs level 7+, 6 other nodes in this tree, and this must be your primary or secondary tree)#

  • Deadeye. Your ranged attacks (weapons, Spit, Mind Spike, ranged Surges) Crit on 18–20. Once per round, Push to reroll a missed attack.

Evolution nodes (Oracle only; granted automatically)#

  • Foresight (level 4, Evolution I). A lidless third eye opens. At the start of each round, roll a d20 and set it aside: your Omen. Once before the round ends, after any d20 is rolled by you or an ally within 60 ft, you may replace that roll with the Omen. An unused Omen fades at the end of the round.
  • Thousand Eyes (level 7, Evolution II). Eyes open all over you. Target Lock can mark up to three creatures at once. You and allies within 60 ft can't be surprised or Blinded. Your ranged attacks ignore partial cover, and their Crit range is one wider than it would otherwise be: 20 → 19–20, 19–20 → 18–20, 18–20 → 17–20. This is an exception to the rule that Crit ranges don't stack.

Glands — the walking pharmacy#

Bio: venom sacs, acid glands, healing bile, spore pods. Chrome: chem injectors, nanite reservoirs, drug pumps, nozzle ports.

Stat: Gumption · Role: chemist, healer, attrition · Unlocks: Burst (Shape), Toxin, Corrode, Mend · Primary tree of: Alembic · Tertiary of: Juggernaut

← Augment Trees

Root#

  • Spit. A ranged natural attack (d8, 30 ft, Nerve or Gumption) dealing Toxin or Corrode damage (choose each time). Advantage on Endure against poison.

Tier I (needs the Root)#

  • Regenerate. At the start of your turn, if you're at half HP or less (and not Down), regain Rank + 1 HP.
  • Stim Gland. Action (or Quick with Push): you or a creature you touch regains Rank d6 + Gumption HP and ends Burning or Poisoned. Twice per Breather.
  • Adrenal Dump. The first time each combat you drop to half HP or less, gain 2 × Rank + Grit temporary HP and advantage on your next attack.
  • Antibodies. You can't be Poisoned. Quick, once per Breather: end one condition on a creature you touch.

Tier II (needs level 4+ and 3 nodes in this tree)#

  • Purge. Once per combat, Quick: lose Flux equal to Rank + 1 and take that much damage (ignores Armor).
  • Catalyst. Your Burst Surges roll d8 damage dice instead of d6.
  • Spore Cloud. Action, once per combat, Push: exhale a 15-ft-radius cloud centred on you that lasts until the end of next round. Creatures outside it can't see into it. You and your allies inside are Veiled against attacks made from outside the cloud.
  • Mutagen Tap. Once per round, when you would gain Flux, you may take Rank + 1 damage per point instead (ignores Armor; it can't drop you below 1 HP).

Apex (needs level 7+, 6 other nodes in this tree, and this must be your primary or secondary tree)#

  • Living Pharmacy. Stim Gland affects you and every ally within 15 ft at once. Your Mend Surges cost no Flux.

Evolution nodes (Alembic only; granted automatically)#

  • Transmute (level 4, Evolution I). Your glands learn to brew anything. When your Toxin or Corrode damage applies its rider, the target is both Poisoned and Exposed. Your healing (Stim Gland, Mend Surges, Patch) restores +Gumption HP.
  • Panacea (level 7, Evolution II). Your blood is medicine. Once per combat, Action: you and every ally within 30 ft regain (Rank + 1)d8 + Gumption HP, end all conditions, and lose 2 Flux. A Down ally stands up.

Wiring — faster than you should be#

Bio: hyper-fast nerves, eel-organs, adrenal crystals. Chrome: reflex boosters, synthetic muscle, capacitor banks, plasma coils.

Stat: Moxie · Role: speed, reflexes, shock · Unlocks: Shock, Blaze, Haste · Primary tree of: Skitter · Secondary of: Siren · Tertiary of: Oracle

← Augment Trees

Root#

  • Quickened. +10 ft speed. You can Dash as a Quick action. Your group has advantage on initiative checks.

Tier I (needs the Root)#

  • Reflex Spike. Reaction, Push: when you succeed on a Dodge against a melee attack, make one weapon attack against the attacker with half the damage dice (round up).
  • Capacitor. Once per turn when you hit with a melee attack, deal +1 damage die (one more of that attack's dice) as Shock. Push: the target is also Dazed.
  • Slipstream. You never provoke Opportunity Strikes, can move through enemies' spaces, and take no damage when you succeed on a Dodge against an Area attack.
  • Wall Run. As part of your Move you can run along walls and across liquids, as long as you end the Move on something that holds you (otherwise you fall).

Tier II (needs level 4+ and 3 nodes in this tree)#

  • Overclock. Once per Breather, take one extra Action on your turn, then gain 1 Flux.
  • Arc Jump. Once per turn, as part of your Move, flash up to 20 ft in a straight line, passing through creatures' spaces. Push: each creature you pass through takes 2 × Rank Shock damage.
  • Kinetic Battery. Each time you succeed on a Dodge, store a charge (max 3). When you hit with an attack, you may spend all your charges: +1 damage die per charge, as Shock. Charges fade when combat ends.
  • Afterimage. When you Dash, you are Veiled until the start of your next turn.

Apex (needs level 7+, 6 other nodes in this tree, and this must be your primary or secondary tree)#

  • Blur. You get two Moves each turn. If you've moved 20+ ft this turn, roll your first Dodge each round with advantage until your next turn.

Evolution nodes (Skitter only; granted automatically)#

  • Mantis Reflex (level 4, Evolution I). Your nerves fire before you think. You get two Reactions per round (both refresh at the start of your turn). Your Reflex Spike and Opportunity Strikes use your full damage dice.
  • Lightning Step (level 7, Evolution II). You move between moments. Once per turn, after you Unleash a Surge, you may make one weapon attack as a Quick action, with half its damage dice (round up).

Mind — the voice in every head#

Bio: swollen cortex, psionic nodules, pheromone glands, a voice that echoes. Chrome: neural coprocessor, wetware deck, voice modulator, antenna crown.

Stat: Chutzpah · Role: psionics, hacking, control, leadership · Unlocks: Dread, Link · Primary tree of: Siren · Secondary of: Oracle · Tertiary of: Alembic

← Augment Trees

Root#

  • Uplink. Speak mind-to-mind (Bio) or by encrypted radio (Chrome) with willing creatures within 300 ft. Mind Spike: a ranged attack (d8, 60 ft, Nerve or Chutzpah) dealing Psychic damage.

Tier I (needs the Root)#

  • Intrude. Action: Gumption or Chutzpah + Rank vs a creature's TN (or a device's DC). Read its surface thoughts, or seize an unattended device for 1 minute. In combat, a Mook machine obeys you until the end of next round; any other machine is Dazed.
  • Iron Will. Advantage on Resist, and you can't be Shaken. Allies within 30 ft get +1 to Resist.
  • Commanding Voice. You can Rally as a Quick action.
  • Read the Room. Advantage on checks to spot a lie. Once per scene, ask the GM what a creature you can see wants or fears most right now; the answer is true.

Tier II (needs level 4+ and 3 nodes in this tree)#

  • Puppet. Action, Push: Chutzpah + Rank vs the TN of a non-Boss creature. On a success, it immediately does one of these, your choice: moves up to its speed where you choose, or makes one attack against a target you choose. An enemy target simply takes the attack's Damage (no roll, no rider); a player target defends normally.
  • Precog. Reaction, Push: when you or an ally within 30 ft is about to make a d20 roll (declare before rolling), they roll it with advantage.
  • Psychic Scream. Action, once per combat: make one Chutzpah attack (an Area attack) against every enemy within 30 ft that you choose. Hit: (Rank + 1)d6 Psychic and Shaken. Miss: half damage.
  • Glamour. Quick, Push: you are Veiled until the end of next round.

Apex (needs level 7+, 6 other nodes in this tree, and this must be your primary or secondary tree)#

  • Hive Mind. Once per round, an ally within 300 ft can use your Nerve or Chutzpah in place of theirs for one roll. At the start of each combat, choose one ally: they Prime one extra Surge.

Evolution nodes (Siren only; granted automatically)#

  • Siren Song (level 4, Evolution I). Your voice splits into harmonies. Once per round you can Taunt as a Quick action, and your Taunt can target every enemy within 30 ft you choose (compare one roll to each creature's TN). Each enemy you Taunt this way must target you or one ally you name within 30 ft of you (same ally for all of them) if it can, and has −2 TN against that creature's defense rolls until the Taunt ends.
  • Crown of Will (level 7, Evolution II). Once per combat, Action, Push: Chutzpah + Rank vs the TN of a creature within 60 ft. A non-Boss obeys you until the end of combat. In each Enemy Phase it acts as you choose (it won't harm itself), and it breaks free if you or an ally damages it. A Boss instead loses its next Interrupt and is Dazed until the end of its next turn.

4. Surges & the Sequence#

Mutagen doesn't take orders well. In a fight, your body offers you a few of its powers at random: a spurt of acid, a crackle of arc-light, a shell that snaps shut. These are Surges. They are optional. Your weapons and Augments always work; Surges are the big, unreliable spikes on top.

The Short Version#

  1. You build Surges from parts and write them on your Sequence (a numbered list).
  2. At the start of each fight you Prime: roll your Sequence die a few times. The Surges you roll are ready.
  3. On your turn you may Unleash a Primed Surge as your Action. It costs Flux.
  4. Want more options? Churn as a Quick action to roll again.
  5. From your first Evolution (level 4) you also have Signature Surges that are always ready (below).

Building a Surge#

A Surge = one Shape + one Effect (+ optional Twist). Name it and describe what it looks like. Bolt + Corrode might be "Acid Spit" for a Bio freelancer or "Etching Laser" for a Chrome one.

You can use any base part, plus parts unlocked by trees you have the Root of.

Shapes (how it's delivered)#

ShapeUnlockTargetAttack statDamage on hit
StrikebaseOne creature in melee reachGrit or Moxie(Rank+1)d10 + stat
BoltbaseOne creature within 60 ftNerve(Rank+1)d8 + stat
BurstGlandsEverything in a 10-ft radius within 60 ftNerve(Rank+1)d6
WaveLimbs15-ft cone or 30-ft line from youGrit or Nerve(Rank+1)d6
PulseHideAny creatures you choose within 10 ft of youGrit(Rank+1)d6
InfusebaseYou or one ally within 30 ft— (no roll)Uses an Infuse Effect

Area Shapes (Burst, Wave, Pulse): roll one attack and compare it to each target's Guard. Hit: full damage + Effect. Miss: half damage, no Effect. Allies in a Burst or Wave are hit too (they roll Dodge against your attack total; success = half damage, no rider); a Pulse hits only the creatures you choose. Footprints on a grid (a 10-ft radius is 5×5 squares, a 15-ft cone is 3 squares deep) are in Combat.

Attack stat. A Surge uses its Shape's attack stat, or the stat of the tree that unlocked its Effect, whichever you prefer:

Effect's treeHideLimbsSensesGlandsWiringMind
Stat it allowsGritGrit or MoxieNerveGumptionMoxieChutzpah

Bolt + Shock can use Nerve (Bolt) or Moxie (Wiring); Burst + Toxin can use Nerve or Gumption (Glands); Wave + Dread can use Grit, Nerve or Chutzpah (Mind). Base Effects (Kinetic) use the Shape's stat only.

Effects (what it does)#

Damage Effects go with Strike, Bolt, Burst, Wave, or Pulse. The rider applies on a hit (conditions are in Combat).

EffectUnlockDamage typeRider on hit
KineticbaseKinetic+1 damage die, and you may push the target 10 ft
BlazeWiringBlazeBurning
ShockWiringShockDazed
ToxinGlandsToxinPoisoned
CorrodeGlandsCorrodeExposed
SnareLimbsKineticHeld
QuakeHideKineticProne (not Huge)
GlareSensesBlazeBlinded
DreadMindPsychicShaken

Infuse Effects go only with Infuse. No roll, no miss.

EffectUnlockWhat happens
MendGlandsTarget regains (Rank+1)d8 + Gumption HP and ends Burning and Poisoned. A Down target stands up.
ShellHideTarget gains (Rank+1)d6 + Grit temporary HP and +1 Armor until the end of next round.
HasteWiringAn ally (not you) immediately takes a Move and one Action (not Unleash), with advantage on any roll that Action needs.

Twists (optional, +1 Flux each)#

A Surge can carry one Twist (two different Twists from Rank 3). Each Twist adds +1 Flux to its cost. Twists are always available.

TwistWorks withEffect
ChainStrike, BoltAfter resolving, repeat it against a second target within 15 ft of the first for half damage.
LingerBurst, Wave, PulseThe area stays until the end of next round. An enemy that enters it or starts its turn there takes 2 × Rank damage and the rider (no roll).
LeechAny damageRegain HP equal to half the damage dealt to one target.
OverchargeAny damage+2 damage dice.
SureAnyRoll the attack with advantage, or Infuse one extra ally.
ReachAnyDouble range or area size. Strike reaches 15 ft.
HushAnySilent and invisible in origin; using it doesn't reveal you or break stealth.

Budget check. A plain weapon hit at level 1 averages ~7.5 damage (1d8 + 3). A Bolt Surge averages ~12 and applies a condition. At level 7 (Rank 4, primary +8) a weapon hit is ~26 and a Bolt Surge ~30.5 plus a rider. That's the trade: Surges are stronger, but you don't choose which ones you get (except your Signatures), and each one pushes you toward Overload.

The Sequence#

Your Sequence is a numbered list of your Surges. Its size is your Sequence die. The die only grows twice after level 2, when you Evolve:

Level12–34–6 (Evolution I)7–10 (Evolution II)
Sequence died4d6d8d12
Surges knownlevel + 2 (3 at level 1, 12 at level 10)
Prime2234
Signature Surges——12
Wild slots12, then 12, 1, 03, 2, 1, 0

Write your Surges in slots 1, 2, 3... Any slot without a Surge is Wild (see below). Right after each Evolution your new body offers powers you don't understand yet (extra Wild slots). Then you fill them in, one per level, until your Sequence is full at levels 6 and 10.

You can leave a slot Wild on purpose. When you gain a level, you may rewrite one known Surge into a different build.

Priming#

At the start of each combat (after initiative), each freelancer rolls their Sequence die once per point of Prime. Each result's Surge is Primed: ready to Unleash this fight. Mark them.

  • Doubles: if two dice show the same Surge, it is Primed once and Amped: it costs 0 Flux when Unleashed.
  • Wild: if a die shows a Wild slot, roll on the Wild Surge table right away. That result is Primed. Each Wild die rolls separately; Wild results never count as doubles.
  • Juice: spend 1 Juice to set one Sequence die to any result before you check for doubles.
  • Chrome Firmware (see Augment Trees) lets you swap one Primed Surge after rolling.

Unused Primed Surges fade when combat ends.

Unleashing#

Unleash is an Action. Choose a Primed Surge, pay its Flux (1 + 1 per Twist; 0 if Amped), and resolve it. It is no longer Primed.

Missed? If a Strike or Bolt Surge misses, the Flux is still paid but the Surge stays Primed (still Amped, if it was). Your body tried; it'll try again.

Churning#

Churn is a Quick action: gain 1 Flux and roll your Sequence die once; that Surge is Primed (doubles with an already Primed Surge make it Amped). You can't Churn on a turn you Unleash (before or after); a Misfire's free Churn is the only exception. You can't hold more Primed Surges than Prime + 1 (Signature Surges don't count); if you would, choose which to drop.

Signature Surges#

At Evolution I (level 4) you gain one Signature Surge, and at Evolution II (level 7) a second. These are the powers your evolved body was built around.

  • Build each from your parts like any Surge, with the Twists your Rank allows, and write it in a Signature box, not on the Sequence. It doesn't count toward Surges known, Prime, or the Primed maximum.
  • Always ready: it's Primed at the start of every combat. When you Unleash it, it is Primed again at the start of your next turn, so you can Unleash each Signature once per round.
  • Cost: its normal Flux (1 + 1 per Twist). Doubles can't Amp it. Only Emergence (its first use) and Final Form make it free. Firmware can't swap it.
  • Missed Strike or Bolt Signatures are simply ready again next turn.
  • When you level up (from level 5), you may rebuild one Signature Surge.

Why it's fair: you still get one Action a turn, and every Unleash costs Flux. A freelancer who Unleashes a Signature every round Overloads about once every two fights, unless they have a high Flux Limit (Oracles) or take a turn off to swing a weapon.

Surges Outside Combat#

In any tense scene where the GM calls for initiative-style timing (a chase, a heist gone loud), Surges work the same way. In calm scenes you can't Prime; the Mutagen only answers when you're afraid.

Wild Surge Table (d12)#

When a Wild slot is Primed, roll here. Unless it says otherwise, it costs 1 Flux to Unleash like any Surge.

d12Wild Surge
1Misfire. Your body sputters. This slot isn't Primed; instead, immediately Churn once for free (no Flux, no action).
2Spore Bloom. Burst + Toxin with +2 dice, centred on you (you're unaffected). Allies in it roll Dodge.
3Arc Storm. Bolt + Shock that hits up to three targets at full damage. You are Dazed afterward.
4Hardening. Shell on you and every ally within 10 ft. Your speed is 0 until your next turn.
5Blood Price. Strike + Kinetic with +2 more dice. You take Rank d6 damage (ignores Armor).
6Echo. Unleash a copy of any Surge an ally currently has Primed (it stays Primed for them).
7Mitosis. A shuddering copy of you appears adjacent. It acts on your turn (Move + one weapon attack, using your numbers). When an enemy attacks it, you roll Dodge for it; any failure destroys it. It melts at the end of combat.
8Phase Step. Teleport up to 60 ft, then Strike + Kinetic a creature next to you.
9Gravity Knot. Burst with both Quake and Snare riders.
10Feedback. Pulse + Dread with a 20-ft radius. Costs 2 Flux.
11Flush. Costs 0 Flux. Set your Flux to 0 and regain Rank d8 HP.
12Perfect Expression. Unleash it as a Quick action for 0 Flux: Prime any two of your Surges as Amped (this can exceed your Primed maximum).

Steal these, rename them, or build your own.

NameBuildFluxNotes

5. Flux & Overload#

Every Surge, every Push, every Churn floods your cells (or circuits) with Mutagen. Flux measures how close you are to losing control.

Flux#

  • Your Flux starts each mission at 0 (Chrome freelancers who skipped Upkeep start higher).
  • You gain Flux when you:
    • Unleash a Surge: 1, +1 per Twist (0 if Amped).
    • Churn: 1.
    • Push an Augment: 1.
    • Fail your defense against a Mutagenic threat's attack: as its stat block says.
  • Your Flux Limit = 4 + Rank + Nerve (minimum 4; Splice −1). Nerve rises at each Evolution, so your Limit does too: from 4–8 at level 1 to 9–16 at level 7 (one less for a Splice), highest for Oracles and lowest for Sirens.
  • Signature Surges cost Flux like any Surge. Unleashing one every round is the fastest way to Overload; that's the price of always being ready.
  • Flux drops to 0 when you take a Breather or a Lockdown, and when you Overload.
  • Flux never stops you from acting. You can always choose to go over.

Overload#

The moment your Flux goes above your Limit, you Overload:

  1. Take Rank d6 damage (ignores Armor). Overload damage (including Glitch Short) can't drop you below 1 HP; if you're already Down, skip it.
  2. Roll d12 on your Material's table: Bloom if all your trees are Bio, Glitch if all are Chrome. Splices roll both and pick one.
  3. Set your Flux to 0.

Results last until the end of your next turn unless they say otherwise. Scars and Faults are permanent.

Why go over? Sometimes the fight is worth it. An Overload resets your Flux and the table has a few gifts. Most results hurt, though, and doing it twice in a fight is a good way to end up Down.

Bloom Table (Bio)#

d12Result
1Scar. A permanent, uncontrolled mutation. Roll on the Scar table below.
2Seizure. You fall Prone and are Dazed.
3Ravenous. Disadvantage on checks (not attacks or defenses) until you eat a ration.
4Overgrowth. Your speed is halved until your next Breather.
5Red Mist. On your next turn you must attack the nearest creature, friend or foe.
6Fever. You are Poisoned.
7Molt. Armor −1 until your next Breather, but regain Rank d8 HP now.
8Twitch. One random Surge you know (roll your Sequence die; Wild = nothing) becomes Primed.
9Adrenal Flood. Gain 2 × Rank temporary HP. You are Shaken.
10Cocoon. You are Held (encased) until the end of your next turn, but take no damage until then.
11Blossom. A beautiful permanent change: gain one new Knack describing it (Bioluminescent, Smells Like Rain...).
12Flowering. One Primed Surge becomes Amped, and gain 1 Juice.

Glitch Table (Chrome)#

d12Result
1Fault. A permanent malfunction. Roll on the Fault table below.
2Hard Reboot. You lose your next Action.
3Short. Take another Rank d6 Shock damage.
4Joint Lock. Your speed is 0.
5Targeting Error. Your next attack targets a random creature in range (the GM picks among friends and foes).
6Blackout. You are Blinded.
7Heat Vent. Every creature within 10 ft of you, ally or enemy, takes Rank d6 Blaze (allies Dodge vs DC 12 + Rank to avoid).
8Log Dump. Numbers scroll past your eyes: you Analyze one enemy for free.
9Safe Mode. +1 Armor until combat ends, but your Surges cost +1 Flux until combat ends.

Scars and Faults (d6)#

Permanent, but survivable. A clinic can remove one for 200 Scrip between missions.

d6Bio ScarChrome Fault
1Weeping Pores. You leave a trail; disadvantage on stealth checks against smell-trackers.Tick. Your chrome clicks audibly; disadvantage on stealth checks against hearing.
2Wrong Face. Unaugmented people are unsettled; disadvantage on Chutzpah checks to charm them (advantage to intimidate).Static Voice. Same, but through a speaker grille.

6Hunger for Change. Gain +1 Flux at the start of every combat. Your first Surge each combat is Amped.Feedback Loop. Gain +1 Flux at the start of every combat. Your first Surge each combat is Amped.

Last Gasp#

Once per Lockdown, when you would drop to 0 HP, you may Overload on purpose instead: skip the damage step, roll on your table, and stay at 1 HP. Your body refuses to die, and pays for it.

Mutagenic Threats#

Some enemies are Mutagenic (see Threats). When you fail your defense against their attack, you also gain the listed Flux (a successful defense against an Area keeps it out, even though you take half damage). This is how the city slowly changes you.

6. Combat#

Combat is fast because the GM barely rolls. Players attack enemies' Guard; players defend against enemies' TN. Enemies move together, so the GM resolves them in one sweep.

Starting a Fight#

  1. Who goes first?
    • If the freelancers start it (ambush, first shot), players go first.
    • If enemies ambush, the group makes a Nerve group check (notice) vs the enemies' highest TN. Failure: enemies take a free Enemy Phase first; after it, players go first.
    • Otherwise, the group makes a Moxie group check vs the enemies' highest TN. Success: players go first. Failure: enemies go first.
  2. Prime. Every freelancer rolls their Sequence dice (Surges).
  3. Run rounds.

The Round#

Each round has two phases:

  1. Player Phase. Players take turns in any order they agree on, one at a time. A player can wait and go later in the phase, as long as they haven't done anything yet this turn.
  2. Enemy Phase. Every enemy gets a Move and one action (usually an attack; Elites attack twice, Bosses see Threats). The GM resolves the enemies one at a time, in any order; targeted players roll defense. At the start of each enemy's turn, first resolve what happens "at the start of its turn": Burning, Regenerating, and a Boss ending one condition on itself.

Then the next round starts. If enemies went first, the round is Enemy Phase then Player Phase.

Durations. "Until the end of its next turn" means the end of that creature's next turn. For enemies, their turn is the Enemy Phase, so a condition you put on an enemy during the Player Phase lasts through the coming Enemy Phase and ends when that phase ends. "Until the end of next round" means through the whole round after the current one.

Bosses' Interrupts. A Boss also gets an Interrupt: one action (no Move) right after any player's turn, once per round (Threats).

Your Turn#

On your turn you get a Move, an Action, and a Quick action, in any order. You also get one Reaction per round (it refreshes at the start of your turn; the Skitter's Mantis Reflex gives two).

Move. Up to your speed (30 ft; 6 squares on a grid). You can split it around your Action. Climbing, swimming, crawling, and difficult terrain cost double. Standing from Prone costs half your speed.

Actions#

ActionWhat it does
AttackWeapon or natural attack: d20 + stat + Rank vs Guard. Damage = Rank × weapon die + stat.
UnleashUse a Primed Surge or a Signature Surge (Chapter 4).
DashMove again.
BraceAdvantage on all defense rolls until your next turn.
HelpAn ally within 30 ft gets advantage on their next roll before your next turn. Describe how.
PatchUse a Medkit charge on a creature you touch: Gumption check, DC 10. Success: it regains Rank d6 + Gumption HP (a Down creature stands up). Failure: the charge is still used, but it regains 1 HP.
AnalyzeGumption + Rank vs the TN of a creature you can see within 60 ft. Success: learn its stat block (or one weakness) and it is Exposed until the end of its next turn.
TauntChutzpah + Rank vs the TN of a creature you can see within 60 ft. Success: in its next Enemy Phase, it must target you if it can.
RallyChutzpah check, DC 13. Success: every ally within 60 ft who can hear you gains Rank + Chutzpah temporary HP. Once per combat per ally.
Grapple / ShoveGrit + Rank vs the Guard of a creature in your melee reach. Success: the target is Held, or pushed 10 ft, or knocked Prone (not Huge).
OtherHack a door, haul a lever, run a check. If it takes about 6 seconds, it's an Action.

Quick Actions#

Draw or stow an item, open a door, drink a stim, speak a few sentences, Churn, Target Lock (Senses), or anything the rules call Quick.

Reactions#

You have one Reaction per round. Spend it on:

  • Opportunity Strike: when an enemy leaves your melee reach, make one melee weapon attack against it.
  • Reactions from Augments (Bulwark, Reflex Spike, Threat Sense, Precog, Fortress).

Opportunity Strikes#

  • Leaving reach provokes. When a creature moves out of an enemy's melee reach, that enemy may make one melee attack against it right then (a freelancer attacks with a melee weapon; an enemy uses its melee attack and you defend).
  • One per round. A freelancer's Opportunity Strike uses their Reaction. Each enemy can make one Opportunity Strike per round. A Dazed creature can't make one.
  • Moving carefully: move at half speed (each 5 ft costs 10 ft; each square costs 2) and you provoke no Opportunity Strikes for that movement.
  • Teleporting, being pushed or pulled, and Slipstream never provoke.

Positioning: Theatre of the Mind or Grid#

Mutagen plays equally well with theatre of the mind or on a battle map. Pick one per table (or per fight). Every distance in the book is in feet; this is how to read it either way.

DistanceTheatre of the mindGrid (1 square = 5 ft)
Touch, adjacent, melee reachClose1 square, diagonals included
Reach 10 ft (Huge, Grapnel, Pole Haft)Close, or one step away2 squares
30 ft (one Move, Help, Infuse, Shotgun)Near6 squares
60 ft (Bolt, Burst, Pistol, Analyze, Taunt, Rally)Far12 squares
120 ft (Rifle, a Bolt with Reach)Far24 squares
BeyondDistantoff the map

Ranges (both ways)#

  • Melee reach is 5 ft (adjacent) unless a feature extends it.
  • Ranged attacks reach their listed range. You can shoot up to double that range with disadvantage, except with Area weapons, grenades and Surges (those stop at their listed range).
  • A shooter next to an enemy is distracted. Ranged attacks are at disadvantage while an enemy is adjacent to the attacker. When an enemy fires a ranged attack while a freelancer is adjacent to it, the target defends with advantage.
  • Line of sight: you need to see a target to attack it at range or to Analyze, Taunt or Target Lock it. Creatures don't block sight; walls and big obstacles do.
  • Pushes move the target directly away from you.

Areas (both ways)#

An Area hits every creature inside it; each one rolls its own defense (enemies compare your one attack to their Guard).

  • Burst "N-ft radius" (or "N ft around it"): every creature within N ft of a point. On a grid, a square of N÷5 squares around the point: a 10-ft burst covers 5×5 squares, 20 ft covers 9×9. "Around it" leaves out the creature itself.
  • Cone N ft: from you, N÷5 squares deep, widening one square on each side per square (a quarter-circle).
  • Line N ft: from you, N÷5 squares long and one square wide.
  • Walls stop Areas. A square the centre of the Area can't see is not in it.
  • Allies in your Area: your Burst and Wave hit allies inside too (they roll Dodge against your attack total; success = half damage, no rider). Pulses, Psychic Scream and anything that says "creatures you choose" hit only who you choose.
  • Who's in it, theatre of the mind: the GM decides from the fiction. As a guide for a party of four that isn't bunching up or spreading out, a 10-ft Area catches its target and about one in three of the others, 20 ft about half, 30 ft about two in three. Tell the players when they're bunched up.

On a Grid#

  • Distance is the larger of the two gaps (diagonals count as one square).
  • Every creature fills one square, Huge ones included (or 2×2 if your map has room). You can move through allies but not enemies, and you can't end your move in an occupied square.
  • Walls and big obstacles block movement, line of sight and Areas (trace a line from centre to centre). Fliers ignore obstacles when moving.
  • Summoned creatures appear in free squares next to their summoner.

Attacking#

Roll d20 + stat + Rank against the target's Guard.

  • Melee: the stat listed for the weapon in Gear (Grit for heavy hitting, Moxie for finesse; many weapons allow either).
  • Ranged: Nerve. Long range (up to double, with disadvantage) and shooting with an enemy next to you: see Ranges.
  • Crit on a natural 20: roll the damage dice twice.

Defending#

When an enemy attacks you, roll d20 + defense stat + Rank against its TN. The stat block names the defense:

  • Dodge (Moxie): claws, bullets, spit, anything you can see coming.
  • Endure (Grit): gas, blasts, disease, crushing grabs.
  • Resist (Nerve): fear, psychic attacks, hacking your wetware.

Single attacks: success = no damage. Area attacks: success = half damage. Failure = full damage plus any rider.

Enemy Opportunity Strikes. If you leave an enemy's melee reach on your turn, it gets a free attack on you right then (you defend; one per enemy per round, above). Move carefully (half speed) to slip away safely.

Damage#

  • Armor reduces each instance of damage by its value (minimum 1). Armor doesn't reduce Psychic damage or anything that "ignores Armor."
  • Resistance halves damage of a type; Vulnerability doubles it.
  • Temporary HP soaks damage first and doesn't stack (keep the higher). It fades at the end of combat.
  • Cover: partial cover gives you +2 to defense rolls (and gives enemies +2 Guard). Full cover means you can't be targeted.
  • Damage types: Kinetic, Blaze, Shock, Toxin, Corrode, Psychic.

Conditions#

All conditions last until the end of the affected creature's next turn unless a rule says otherwise. Reapplying a condition refreshes it; it doesn't stack. Bosses end one condition on themselves at the start of their turn in every Enemy Phase.

ConditionEffect
BlindedCan't see. Disadvantage on attacks (a Blinded enemy's targets defend with advantage); attacks against it have advantage (a Blinded player defends with disadvantage).
BurningTakes 2 × the source's Rank Blaze damage at the start of its next turn (for enemies: at the start of its turn in the Enemy Phase), then the flames die down. Healing that ends Burning (Mend, Stim Gland) puts it out before it bites.
DazedNo Reaction or Quick action (so no Opportunity Strikes). A Dazed enemy can't use Specials, and a Dazed Boss gets only one action.
Exposed−2 Guard (enemies) or −2 to defense rolls (players).
HeldSpeed 0. Ends early if the holder is moved away, Dazed, or Down.
PoisonedDeals half damage.
ProneMelee attacks against it have advantage; ranged attacks against it have disadvantage. Standing costs half speed.
ShakenDisadvantage on attacks and checks; can't willingly move closer to the source. A Shaken enemy's targets defend with advantage.
VeiledAdvantage on defense rolls and on its next attack.
DownSee below.

Enemy advantage → player disadvantage. Since enemies don't roll, "attacks against a Prone player have advantage" means that player defends with disadvantage.

Going Down#

At 0 HP you are Down: fall Prone, drop what you're holding, and you can only crawl 5 ft and speak.

  • At the end of each Enemy Phase, roll Endure (DC 10). Failure: mark a Death mark. A natural 20: stand up with 1 HP.
  • You can still be attacked while Down; you defend normally (Prone: disadvantage against melee). Taking damage while Down marks a Death mark (two on a Crit or failed defense vs a Boss).
  • 3 Death marks: you die.
  • Any healing stands you up with that much HP. Death marks clear on a Breather.
  • When you go Down, roll on the Injury table. Injuries last until your next Lockdown.
  • Last Gasp (Chapter 5) can keep you up once per Lockdown.
  • If every freelancer is Down or dead, the fight is lost. The enemies win the scene: the GM decides what they do with the fallen (capture, strip their gear, drag them off as Samples, or leave them for dead with their Endure rolls still running). It's a setback, not automatically the end.

Injury Table (d6)#

d6Injury (until Lockdown)
1Cracked Ribs. −5 Max HP.
2Concussion. Disadvantage on Gumption checks.
3Torn Limb. Disadvantage on attacks with one chosen limb (your choice: arms or legs → speed −10 ft instead).
4Ruptured Gland / Fried Port. Your Flux Limit is −2.
5Shell Shock. Disadvantage on Resist.
6Lucky Break. Just a scar. No effect.

Ending a Fight#

Combat ends when one side is gone, flees, or gives up. Unused Primed Surges fade, temporary HP fades, and Bio freelancers' Knit heals them (a Down freelancer healed this way gets up). Enemies at half HP or less with a sense of self-preservation usually try to flee or surrender; at the GM's call, a Chutzpah check can make them.

7. Advancement#

One mission, one level. When the party completes a GRAFT contract (successfully or not, as long as they survive and learn something), everyone gains a level. A full campaign is 10 missions: levels 1 to 10, with the finale played at level 10. For shorter games, start at level 4 (freshly Evolved) or level 7.

Level Table#

LevelRankStageStats (prim / sec / tert / dumps)Nodes: primary + sec/tert (+ Evolution)Surges knownSeq. diePrimeSignaturesOther
11Base+3 / +2 / +1 / +0, −13 + 3 = 63d42—3 Knacks
21Base4 + 4 = 84d62—
32Base5 + 5 = 105d62—+1 Knack
42Evolution I+5 / +3 / +2 / +1, +06 + 6 (+1) = 136d831Evolution node; Tier II opens
53Evolution I7 + 7 (+1) = 157d831Plating → +2 Armor; 2 Twists per Surge

84Evolution II10 + 10 (+2) = 2210d1242Primary tree full

105Final10 + 14 (+2) = 2612d1242Final Form

"Primary + sec/tert" counts nodes in your primary tree plus nodes in your secondary and tertiary trees combined. From level 9, the primary pick overflows into the secondary or tertiary tree.

Each Level#

  1. +5 Max HP (+2 more with Hide: Thick). Recalculate HP whenever Grit changes.
  2. +1 primary-tree node (automatic; you choose which) and +1 node in your secondary or tertiary tree (chapter 3).
  3. +1 Surge (build it from your parts). You may also rewrite one existing Surge, and from level 5 rebuild one Signature Surge.
  4. Recalculate Rank, Flux Limit, and defenses.
  5. Optionally respec one Augment node.

At level 4 and level 7: Evolve (chapter 2A). Raise your stats to the new stage, add +1 Prime, step up the Sequence die, build a Signature Surge, and write in your Form's Evolution node. You Emerge on screen in the next mission's first fight.

There are no stat boosts. Stats rise only at the Evolutions.

Final Form (level 10): your third and last stage. Once per Lockdown, at the start of a combat, enter Final Form until it ends: primary stat +2, Prime two extra Surges, and every Surge you Unleash is Amped (Signatures too).

Samples#

Bosses and some Elites carry a Sample: a piece of their mutated biology or chrome. After defeating one, a freelancer can harvest it with a Gumption check (DC = its TN). Between missions, a GRAFT clinic can splice it into you for 100 Scrip:

  • It becomes a new Surge in one of your Wild slots. It may use the Boss's signature Shape and Effect even if you haven't unlocked them.
  • If you have no Wild slots, it replaces a Surge you know.

GRAFT technically owns all Samples. Selling one on the black market pays 300 Scrip × its Threat level and is a great way to get a mission about it.

Pay#

GRAFT pays 200 + (100 × mission level) Scrip per freelancer on completion (300 at level 1), plus bonuses the GM sets. See Gear for prices.

Respec and Clinics#

Installing nodes happens off-screen at a clinic between missions. Removing a Scar or Fault costs 200 Scrip (a Clinic Rat pays half; see Origins).

8. Gear#

Gear in Mutagen is modular: every weapon is a Frame plus up to one Mod. Damage always scales with your Rank, so a good knife stays useful all campaign.

Money is Scrip (GRAFT company credit, accepted almost everywhere in Halcyon).

Weapons#

Damage = Rank × die + attack stat. A level 5 Juggernaut (Rank 3, Grit +5 after Evolution I) with a Heavy weapon deals 3d10+5.

Frames#

Area weapons work like area Surges: one attack, compare to each Guard, half damage on a miss. They can't fire at long range. Ranges are in feet; on a grid divide by 5 (Pistol 12 squares, Rifle 24, Shotgun 6, Launcher 18, thrown 4). Other ranged weapons can shoot to double their range with disadvantage (Ranges).

Smart-Link+1 to attack rolls. Counts as Chrome (needs Upkeep: 25 Scrip per mission).

Armor#

Armor reduces each hit by its value. Total Armor (gear + Augments) maxes at 4 (5 with Hide's Unbreakable, 6 with the Juggernaut's Siege Hide). You wear one armor, Light or Heavy, plus an optional Shield.
